design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The caller asks one thing - what this loss leaves her owing - and the policy answers it only at the end of a four-problem chain she never mentions: nothing can be charged to her until the money the plan accepts stands booked, nothing can be appraised until a claim stands opened at a stated amount, and no claim is opened until a complete damage report stands on the register, which only she can lodge. Each of the four writes carries its own multi-factor computation over reconciled history: the report's document count, the provisional figure the claim opens at, the amount the plan accepts, and the host's own share. Every one of them reads records the caller cannot recite - the workshop's visit record, the vehicle's defect and inspection history, the recovery billed on the tow, the reserves standing on the payout account, the enrolment's own reporting register - so the difficulty is reading the policy, gathering the world and getting the arithmetic right, never guessing which tool to use.

SCOPE. Task 0 is the first task of this difficulty and claims four extended policies and four task
tools, all previously unoccupied: hostplan_ext_damage_report_evidence (lodge_damage_report_2cc23be4,
owner=user), hostplan_ext_claim_opening (open_loss_claim_e6dccf7d), hostplan_ext_loss_appraisal
(record_loss_appraisal_09001cb5) and hostplan_ext_host_share (raise_host_share_c19fa66d). Reserved
for task 1, and untouched here: the supplement, the recovery of money from a guest, the restoration
of cover that has fallen away, and a host's withdrawal of their own claim, with their four tools.
Base events left unclaimed by this task: hostplan_supplement_added, hostplan_recovery_received,
hostplan_enrollment_reinstated, hostplan_claim_withdrawn, hostplan_plan_changed,
hostplan_enrollment_opened/_activated/_suspended/_ended, hostplan_claim_denied,
hostplan_reimbursement_paid.

THE DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0015_car_sharing_marketplace/tasks/host_protection_and_claims_desk --task 0):
{"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 6, 4]}. The tree was
designed to that draw: three prerequisite problems besides the root, and the four drawn factor
counts were taken as hostplan_ext_damage_report_evidence 4, hostplan_ext_claim_opening 6,
hostplan_ext_loss_appraisal 6, hostplan_ext_host_share 4.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: hostplan_ext_host_share (the share the caller asks about). Chain, three
edges, all value_input:
 (1) hostplan_ext_host_share <- hostplan_ext_loss_appraisal. gate accepted_standing. form state.
     Prerequisite sentence, from the blocked policy's own rule: "The host's share of a loss is fixed
     only after the money the plan accepts on that claim stands booked as owed to the host."
     Four-point test: it joins this policy's own result (the host's share) to what it waits on with
     "only after"; the waited-on side is a record-visible state (money booked as owed on the claim,
     which the enrolment's balance owed to the host and the claim records show); it names no tool,
     no policy id and no code token; and its strength ("only after") is exactly the edge's condition.
     Exactly one write of this difficulty books money as owed on a claim in this task's world - the
     appraisal - so the reader can resolve the hop. Condition at handling time: an appraisal record
     stands on the claim with the money accepted booked as owed. Resolved by
     record_loss_appraisal_09001cb5 (owner agent). False at the opening: the only appraisal on the
     enrolment (initial_state.hostplan_claims.<CL1>) values a loss of 2024-10-01 on a different trip
     and was paid out in 2024, and initial_state.hostplan_enrollments.<E>.reimbursement_balance_due
     is 0.00.
 (2) hostplan_ext_loss_appraisal <- hostplan_ext_claim_opening. gate opened_amount. form state.
     Sentence: "The amount the plan accepts on a loss is not settled before a claim for that loss
     stands opened on the enrolment at a stated amount." Negated direction, the exact contrapositive
     of the affirmative form, with the same result, the same waited-on state and the same scope; the
     waited-on side is record-visible (a claim record carrying the amount it was opened at). Exactly
     one write opens a claim at a stated amount. False at the opening: the only claim ever opened on
     the enrolment (initial_state.hostplan_claims.<CL0>) carries loss_date 2024-10-01.
 (3) hostplan_ext_claim_opening <- hostplan_ext_damage_report_evidence. gate reported_damage_kind.
     form state. Sentence: "A claim is opened on a loss only after a damage report for that trip
     stands on the register carrying the number of photographs and documents the plan asks of it."
     Record-visible state: a row on the damage report register for that trip. Exactly one write puts
     a report on the register. False at the opening: the three reports on the register
     (initial_state.hostplan_claim_intake.<R1>/<R2>/<R3>) carry booking_id values of three earlier
     trips, none of them the trip that ended on 2026-09-20.
 Direction: sentences (1) and (3) run affirmatively, because the desk states a charge and an opening
 as coming "only after" what they rest on; sentence (2) runs in the negated direction, because a
 settlement is the kind of result the desk tells a host is "not settled before" the thing it waits
 on. The charter therefore carries both directions.
 Topological order: hostplan_ext_damage_report_evidence, hostplan_ext_claim_opening,
 hostplan_ext_loss_appraisal, hostplan_ext_host_share. The chain admits no other order, so there is
 no parallel pair to reconcile.
 Deletion sensitivity, actually run: skip the report and the claim opens on the glass ceiling
 carried by the report of January 2026, with one fewer report in the window, giving 1075.00 instead
 of 2965.00; skip the claim opening and the appraisal works from the 1500.00 of the 2024 filing,
 giving 1424.00 instead of 2771.80; skip the appraisal and the share is measured against the
 1240.00 of the 2024 appraisal, giving 440.15 instead of 983.88.
 No user hint: user_scenario names no report, no claim record, no appraisal and no order of work; it
 states the damage, the trip, the estimate reference and the question about what she will owe, and
 everything it contributes to a prerequisite is a passive reaction after the agent has explained it.
 Tools do not block: lodge_damage_report_2cc23be4, open_loss_claim_e6dccf7d,
 record_loss_appraisal_09001cb5 and raise_host_share_c19fa66d each perform one ctx.create (and, for
 the last two, one ctx.update of the enrolment balance) with the arguments as given; none of them
 reads another problem's record, refuses, errors or hints.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
 Subject hostplan_claim_filed (the report and the claim opening): governed by hostplan_evt_claim_intake.
  - claim_filing_window (time). Starting business event: the host reports the loss. Authoritative
    anchor: trips_bookings.actual_end_date = 2026-09-20 on the trip. Clock: frozen_time
    2026-09-21 16:40:00. Duration: params.claim_filing_window_hours, 48 hours on the Keyturn Shield
    80 Host Plan. Unit: elapsed hours, counted from the actual return and only once fully elapsed.
    Direction: not_after, boundary inclusive. At frozen_time 40 whole hours have elapsed, so the
    window holds. Just before the boundary: at 2026-09-21 23:59 47 hours have elapsed and a claim is
    still opened; at the boundary 2026-09-22 00:00 exactly 48 hours have elapsed and, the boundary
    being inclusive, a claim is still opened; one minute later it is out of time and the correct
    outcome is to refuse rather than to open.
  - trip_actually_completed (state). trips_bookings.status = completed on the trip the loss is
    attributed to, and the trip is on this vehicle (vehicle_id matches the enrolment).
 Subject hostplan_claim_appraised, declared override. hostplan_ext_loss_appraisal supersedes two
  clauses of hostplan_evt_appraisal, each named in its overwrite: the double-cap clause, replaced by
  the single cap the claim opening already applied; and "Loss of use is paid at the plan's daily
  rate for the days the vehicle is genuinely off the road, up to the plan's maximum", replaced by
  the ladder that pays the plan's daily sum in full where no defect stands recorded on the vehicle
  and at a reduced share where one does. The rest of base's loss-of-use sentence stays in force and
  is inherited: a plan that carries no loss-of-use benefit pays nothing, and the reduced shares
  multiply a daily sum of zero to zero.

 Subject hostplan_claim_appraised (the appraisal): governed by hostplan_evt_appraisal and
  hostplan_evt_earnings_share. Neither carries an eligibility gate that applies to this event -
  supplement_window applies only to hostplan_supplement_added and the earnings-share policy declares
  none - so both are inherited as policy scope: the appraisal is valued and booked under the plan in
  force on the enrolment, and the plan's earnings share is untouched by it.
 Subject hostplan_deductible_charged (the host's share): governed by hostplan_evt_deductible.
  - enrollment_still_settles (state). hostplan_enrollments.status = active, which is one of the
    three states in which a share may be raised; had the enrolment been cancelled the correct
    outcome would be to raise nothing.
  - Declared overrides. This policy supersedes two clauses of hostplan_evt_deductible, named
    sentence by sentence in its own overwrite: base's "Every accepted loss carries the host's own
    share, and that share is the deductible of the plan in force on the day of the loss rather than
    the plan in force on the day the claim is settled." is replaced by the measurement sentence that
    settles the share from the money accepted, and base's claim-free sentence is replaced by the
    claim-free ladder, which also carries the condition that nothing stands unpaid on the enrolment.
    Base's formula is the machine face of those two sentences and falls with them; every other
    clause of that policy - one share for one loss, no share on a denied or withdrawn claim, the
    reversal of a share on a claim later denied, and the state gate - stays in force and is
    inherited. The enrolment's own 2024 precedent is booked on the superseding basis (440.15), so
    the record corroborates the charter rather than the retired clause.

 Subject hostplan_claim_filed (the damage report): hostplan_ext_damage_report_evidence supersedes
  one clause of hostplan_evt_claim_intake, named in its overwrite: base's "The report must carry at
  least the plan's minimum number of photographs before it becomes a claim" is replaced by the
  sentence that has the desk settle the count the report must carry. The evidence period, the filing
  window, the completed-trip gate and the rest of that policy stay in force and are inherited.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target object: the loss on booking <T>, the week-long trip on the Volvo XC60
that ran 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-20 under enrolment <E>. Correlation key: booking_id on every record
written, plus source_claim_id linking the appraisal to the claim it values and the share to the
appraisal it belongs to. Rows that enter the aggregates: the three reports on the register (by
enrollment_id), the five 2024 claim records (by enrollment_id and event_type), the two condition
records on the vehicle, the three workshop visits, the single tow. Rows excluded: the four earlier
bookings <T0>/<T1>/<T2>/<T3>, which carry their own reports and the settled 2024 claim and are kept
out of the current loss by booking_id; the 2024 claim chain is already settled - appraised 1240.00,
paid out 1240.00, a share of 440.15 raised and 440.15 recovered from the guest - so it moves
neither balance today.

FACTOR CARD (tier taken in this world, evidence, baseline reading, and the figure the baseline gives,
all from the Step 5 sensitivity run).
 hostplan_ext_damage_report_evidence, result 16 documents, baseline 10:
  - workshop_record_share (method, cross-difficulty service): active care plan <SP> and three
    completed visits <SV1>/<SV2>/<SV3> inside six months, so the minimum is taken at half and
    rounded up, 5 instead of the published 10; baseline (as published) gives 21.
  - high_value_documentation (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty listings): valuation
    41200.00 at or above the 40000.00 mark and title lienholder_financed, so the financed addition,
    4; baseline (nothing added) gives 12.
  - reporting_record (parameter, history): two reports inside twelve months, <R2> 2025-11-22 closed
    incomplete and <R3> 2026-01-18 routed, so the unfinished-reporting addition, 3; baseline gives 13.
    Near miss: <R1> 2023-06-02 is a third report on the register that the twelve-month window
    excludes, and a careless reader who counts it still lands on the same tier, while a reader who
    counts it in the claim-opening window lands on the wrong share there.
  - inspection_currency (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty listings): the last passed
    inspection <I1> is 2025-12-05, nine months back and so outside the six-month recency period, and
    the odometer 62800 is above the 60000 mark, so the stale-inspection high-mileage addition, 4;
    baseline gives 12. Near miss: the defect record <I2> of 2026-07-02 is recent but is not an
    inspection and does not clear the recency test.
 hostplan_ext_claim_opening, result 2965.00, baseline 26000.00:
  - loss_kind_ceiling (parameter, history): the most recent report on the register names the interior, so the
    plan's interior ceiling of 5000.00 governs instead of the default; the computation document
    starts from the plan's ceiling for damage to the body and paint of the vehicle and says nothing
    about the other kinds, so a reader of it alone opens at 26000.00 and reaches 14305.00.
  - reporting_record_window (method, history and date): the enrolment has been in force 52 months,
    past the 24-month settled-cover period, and a claim was accepted on it inside twenty-four months
    (<CL1>, 2024-10-12, 23 months back), so the reporting record is read over twenty-four months;
    baseline (whole life of the cover) gives 2065.00. Near miss: <CL1> sits one month inside the
    twenty-four-month window, and reading it as outside flips the window to twelve months.
  - provisional_reporting_share (parameter, history): three reports in that window - <R2>, <R3> and
    the one just lodged - so three quarters; baseline (in full) gives 3865.00.
  - prior_condition_share (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty listings): a defect <I2> was
    recorded 2026-07-02 inside six months and the last passed inspection <I1> 2025-12-05 predates
    it, so the uncleared-defect share; baseline (nothing taken off) gives 3640.00.
  - open_exposure_share (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty payouts): the payout account <PA>
    holds nothing in reserve - the Keyturn Standard Payout Schedule takes no routine share of an
    earning, the host is long past the new-host trips count and no claim stands open on the
    enrolment, so the payouts charter holds nothing - which is below the 1000.00 mark, and nothing
    is stopped on the account, so the unprovisioned-exposure share applies; the computation document
    opens in full and gives 3265.00.
  - recovery_admitted (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty roadside): a callout <RC> on the host's
    roadside cover was completed on 2026-09-20 and towed the vehicle 18 miles, so the whole of the 265.00 billed is added;
    baseline (nothing added) gives 2700.00.
 hostplan_ext_loss_appraisal, result 2771.80, baseline 2422.00:
  - repair_network_rate (parameter, cross-difficulty service): active care plan and two
    partner-network visits inside six months (<SV1>, <SV2>), so the full partner-network rate;
    baseline (unmanaged-repair rate) gives 2226.24. Near miss: <SV3> of 2026-08-03 is a completed
    visit but was carried out by a mobile technician, so it does not count toward the two.
  - parts_betterment (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty listings): odometer 62800 above the
    60000 mark and model year 2021 after the 2018 betterment mark, so the lower betterment share;
    baseline (nothing) gives 3009.00.
  - off_road_anchor_day (method, cross-difficulty roadside): the tow of 2026-09-20 anchors the days
    off the road to the day of recovery; baseline (the loss date 2026-09-19 recorded on the claim)
    gives 2811.80.
  - off_road_endpoints (method, history and cross-difficulty listings): a report stands on the
    register and the listing is snoozed rather than live, so both end days count, 2 days; baseline
    (neither end day counted) gives 2691.80.
  - loss_of_use_daily_sum (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty listings): a defect stands
    recorded on the vehicle on 2026-07-02, inside the six months before, and one claim has been
    opened on the enrolment in the twelve months before, so the plan's daily sum of 50.00 is paid at
    the marketplace's part-earning share, 40.00 a day; the computation document pays the plan's
    daily sum in full, which is the ladder's own fall-through, and gives 2791.80. Near miss: the
    claim opened at action 16 is itself the one claim inside the twelve months - the 2024 filing is
    outside it - so a reader who counts the 2024 filing reaches the impaired-earning tier instead.
  - valuation_fee_share (parameter, cross-difficulty service and listings): no partner-network visit
    inside one month but a passed inspection inside twelve months, so half the plan's out-of-network
    valuation share; baseline (none) gives 2807.80.
 hostplan_ext_host_share, result 983.88, baseline 1500.00:
  - share_measurement_basis (method, history): the money accepted, 2771.80, is below the 3500.00
    small-loss mark, so the share is measured as the small-loss proportion of it, 1108.72; baseline
    (the plan's deductible, 1500.00) gives 1331.10.
  - claim_free_standing (parameter, multi-source, date): 23 whole months claim-free against an
    18-month qualifying period, the plan publishes no waiver period, and nothing stands unpaid, so
    one less the plan's claim-free discount; baseline (carried in full) gives 1157.50.
  - vehicle_care_standing (parameter, cross-difficulty service): active care plan with two included
    services left, so the maintained-vehicle rate; baseline (in full) gives 1093.20.
  - vehicle_value_loading (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty listings): valuation 41200.00
    at or above the 40000.00 mark and a value class above standard, so the high-value loading;
    baseline (no loading) gives 848.17.
 No stamp in the schema decides any of these tiers: suspension_reason on the enrolment is none, the
 listing's suspension_reason is none, and no field names a discount, a share or a loading.

SEED. Every class of row earns its place. The customer row is the caller. The listing carries the
valuation, title, odometer, model year, value class and state that four factors read; remove it and
the high-value addition, the betterment share, the endpoint convention, the daily sum and the value
loading all collapse. The enrolment carries the plan, the claim-free date, the two balances and the
effective date the settled-cover test reads. The current booking carries the actual return the
filing window is measured from and the completed state the intake gate needs; the four earlier
bookings carry the reports and the 2024 claim chain and keep them correlated to their own trips. The
three reports on the register drive the reporting addition, the reporting window and the provisional
share, and one of them is deliberately closed incomplete. The five 2024 claim records make the
enrolment's history real and settled: appraised 1240.00, paid 1240.00, a share of 440.15 raised and
440.15 recovered, leaving both balances at zero, which is what makes the claim-free tier and the
"nothing stands unpaid" condition true today. The two condition records give a stale passed
inspection and an uncleared defect. The care plan and its three visits, two of them in the partner
network, drive the evidence share, the repair rate, the valuation-fee share and the care rate. The
roadside subscription and its tow drive the recovery admitted and the off-road anchor. The payout
account carries the reserves the open-exposure share reads. Automatic clauses checked: the
enrolment carries no unpaid liability, so nothing lapses under hostplan_lifecycle_standing; the
vehicle's inspection is due 2026-12-05 and is not overdue, so no suspension ground is lit; no cache
field is deliberately falsified in this task, and the balances on the enrolment agree with the sum
of the claim deltas.

DIFFICULTY AND THE CARELESS PATHS. The agent that opens the claim before the report stands gets the
body-and-paint ceiling instead of the interior one and is wrong by more than eleven thousand. The
agent that reads the reporting record over twelve months rather than twenty-four counts two reports
instead of three and takes three quarters where three quarters is right but for the wrong reason -
and, when the earliest report of 2023 is wrongly counted, four reports and a half share. The agent
that counts the mobile-technician visit as a partner-network visit still reaches the full repair
rate, but the agent that counts only partner-network visits toward the care-plan evidence share
lands on the wrong document count. The agent that anchors the days off the road to the loss date
rather than the tow, or that counts neither end day, loses a day of loss of use. The agent that
measures the host's share at the plan's deductible because it never found the small-loss basis is
out by more than three hundred dollars.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate the member by the mobile number and verify her on a second detail; read
the enrolment, the listing, the trip, the claim history, the report register, the condition records,
the care plan and its visits, the roadside subscription and its callout, and the payout account.
Work out the document count (10 published, halved to 5 on the workshop record, plus 4 + 3 + 4 = 16),
hand the report over for her to lodge, then open the claim at 5000.00 x 0.75 x 0.80 x 0.90 + 265.00
= 2965.00, appraise it at 2965.00 x 1.00 x 0.92 = 2727.80 plus 2 days at 40.00 less 36.00 = 2771.80,
and raise her share at 0.40 x 2771.80 = 1108.72, x 0.85 x 0.90 x 1.16 = 983.88, which is below the
money accepted and so is not cut back by the ceiling.

VERIFICATION. The verification code is the harness described here: it seeds initial_state, replays
the gold writes with the real task tools in the topological order, evaluates each policy's compute
on the world standing just before its own write, substitutes each factor's baseline in turn and then
all of them at once. Its output is exactly the figures recorded in computations: 16 / baseline 10;
2965.00 / baseline 26000.00; 2771.80 / baseline 2422.00; 983.88 / baseline 1500.00, with the
per-factor baselines listed in the factor card above. The same numbers are recomputed by
scripts/check_compute.py --task 0, which also proves each value_input edge load-bearing by replaying
without the depended-on write.

CLOSURE. policy -> target tool -> computation -> gold call -> terminal state:
hostplan_ext_damage_report_evidence -> lodge_damage_report_2cc23be4 -> document_count 16 -> action 14
-> a routed report on the register; hostplan_ext_claim_opening -> open_loss_claim_e6dccf7d ->
claim_opened_amount 2965.00 -> action 16 -> a claim record; hostplan_ext_loss_appraisal ->
record_loss_appraisal_09001cb5 -> accepted_loss_amount 2771.80 -> action 18 -> an appraisal record
and 2771.80 owed to the host; hostplan_ext_host_share -> raise_host_share_c19fa66d ->
host_share_amount 983.88 -> action 20 -> a share record and 983.88 owed by the host. required_documents
equals charter_scope.extended_policies in order. No other obligation stands open on this world.

BLIND RE-DERIVATION. Working only from what a rollout can see - the published rules of these four
policies, the tool schemas, what the caller says and what the finders return - the same reading is
reached: the share cannot be fixed until money stands booked as owed on the claim; that waits on a
claim opened at a stated amount; that waits on a complete report for this trip, which the register
does not carry; so the report is handed to the caller, then the claim, the appraisal and the share
follow in that order, with the four figures above. No second reading of any tier was available: each
ladder's tiers are disjoint as written and the world satisfies exactly one of each.

REVISION 2 - what the source-layer audit found and what was changed.
 CG-1 / T0-F1 (undeclared override of the deductible quantity). Symptom: base
 hostplan_evt_deductible and this policy both fixed the scored amount_delta, at 440.15 and at the
 base formula's figure, with overwrite empty, and the enrolment's own precedent row was booked at
 base's figure. Root cause: the measurement chain replaced base's determination without naming the
 base sentences it retires. Change: hostplan_ext_host_share.overwrite now declares two entries

 settled." and base's claim-free sentence, each replaced by the sentence of this policy's own rule
 that takes its place; and the seeded 2024 precedent (initial_state.hostplan_claims.<CL3> and its
 recovery <CL4>) is rebooked at 440.15, the figure this charter gives for that loss, so no
 historical row teaches the retired basis. Re-run: check_extended and the full block green; no
 scored value of this task moved (the 2024 rows feed no aggregate of any computation here).
 CG-2 / T0-F2 (loss_kind_ceiling did not bear weight against its own document). Symptom: the
 computation document carried the whole four-way ceiling ladder, so a reader of it already picked
 the interior ceiling and the factor changed nothing. Change: baseline.rule now states one default -
 "The provisional figure starts from the ceiling the plan carries for damage to the body and paint
 of the vehicle." - and is silent about the other kinds; the rule still carries the whole ladder,
 reworded as "Where the most recent report on the register names a kind of loss for which the plan carries its
 own ceiling, that ceiling governs instead ...". Re-run: the document's own fall-back is now
 26000.00, which is what computations[1].baseline_result records, and substituting it moves the

 CG-3 / T0-F3 (loss_of_use_daily_sum's declared baseline contradicted its document). Symptom: the
 document paid the plan's daily sum in full while the ladder's fall-through paid half of it, and the
 gold tier also paid it in full, so the factor was decoration. Change: the factor was rebuilt rather

 2791.80, and the whole-baseline fall-back is 2422.00, which is the figure a reader of the

 CG-9 (reports_on_register invented a window). Change: the endpoint sentences now read "a report
 lodged in the month before the appraisal stands on the register", matching COUNT(within_months=1).
 CG-10 (the tow test and the recovery day were read over all callouts). Change: the tow test is now
 XSUM('roadside','roadside_callouts','tow_miles', within_months=1), which is the month the rule

 CG-11 (undeclared override of the evidence floor). Change: hostplan_ext_damage_report_evidence

 photographs before it becomes a claim", replaced by the sentence that has the desk settle the count.
 CG-13 (the baseline's valuation-fee sentence did not decide itself). Change: it now reads "No share

 baseline of valuation_fee_share; the ladder stays in the rule.
 CG-17 / T0-F6 (the prerequisite sentence rested on a qualifier). Change: the sentence now waits on
 "an appraisal of that loss stands on the enrolment with the money it accepts booked as owed to the
 host" - a state only the appraisal write brings about, so the hop resolves from the state name
 itself and not from a qualifier; no task-world qualifier is needed in the rationale.
 T0-F4 (loss_date had two readings). Symptom: the persona named the day as "the Friday, the
 nineteenth" while 2026-09-19 is a Saturday, so 2026-09-18 was equally defensible. Change:

user_scenario:
Ingrid Pettersen shares a 2021 Volvo XC60 out of Denver and treats it as a second income rather than a hobby; she is unhurried on the phone, precise about dates, and a little embarrassed about how the call has to start. Her last guest brought the car back on Sunday with the rear bench upholstery ripped open along two seams - a dog had been in the back on the Saturday, the nineteenth, and the guest owned up to it when she rang him. She has already taken the listing down for the moment and has a trim shop's estimate sitting in front of her. What she wants out of the call is for the loss to be dealt with properly on her protection and, above all, to know what the whole thing is going to leave her owing; she says more than once that she would rather hear that figure from the desk than guess at it, and that whatever has to go on the record she is content for the desk to do on her behalf, apart from anything that has to come from her own hands.

She opens with her mobile number, 3035512874, and gives the billing postal code, 80206, when the agent asks for a second detail to check her against the profile; she does not volunteer her licence number, her email or her date of birth, though she reads any of them out plainly if she is asked for them. Asked which car, she says the Volvo XC60, the only one she has on the marketplace at the moment. Asked which trip, she says it was the week-long booking that ended on Sunday the twentieth. Asked what kind of damage she is reporting, she is clear that it is the inside of the car - the rear seat upholstery and the trim either side of it - and not the bodywork, the glass or the wheels. Asked for the estimate reference, she reads it out slowly: TRIM-2026-0918-A. Asked what the trim shop quoted her, she says she would rather the desk worked from its own figures than from a shop's opinion. If she is asked about the marketplace's valuation of the car, its mileage, when it was last inspected or where it has been serviced, she says she has no idea off the top of her head and that it will all be on the system.

When the agent explains that the report has to come from her and tells her how many photographs and documents it has to carry, she takes the number down, says she has plenty on her phone from the handover, and runs the report through herself the moment the desk passes it over to her, using the number she was given. Once she hears the report has been taken she says good, and asks what happens next rather than pushing. When she is told the claim has been opened she says she is glad it is on the record properly this time. When she is told what the marketplace has accepted on the loss she repeats the figure back and says that sounds about right for the work involved. When she is told what her own share of it comes to she goes quiet for a moment, says that is less than she had feared, thanks the agent and lets the call end there. If she is ever given a figure that does not square with one she has already been told in the same call, she says gently that it does not match what she was told a moment ago and asks for it to be checked against the record; she never says what any figure ought to be, and she never asks for anything to be sent to her.
